summary: We developed "Tales of the Abandoned" an interactive storytelling experience that brings NASA's retired and inactive missions back to life. By transforming real archival data and telemetry from spacecraft left behind across the solar system into adaptive, kid-friendly adventures, we tackle declining reading comprehension and short attention spans. Players must read short mission tales carefully to gather clues and solve physics-based challenges, turning passive screen time into active learning. This experience is vital because it bridges the gap between past and future: it honors the forgotten robotic pioneers of the last 50 years while inspiring the next generation of scientists and explorers.
details:
“Tales of the Abandoned” is an interactive storytelling experience that takes children through an intergalactic journey where they are presented with different planets. Each time they select a planet, they will be presented with a series of tasks and stories that they must complete in order to advance in the game. This platform has the intention of promoting reading comprehension, scientific interest, problem solving, and historical knowledge on NASA’s abandoned, but very real missions.

Our project was developed using multiple forms of SI and software, such as Claude, Gemini, Adobe Illustrator, CSS3, Web Audio API, and the coding languages HTML5 and JavaScript.

Claude: Used for refining and structuring the code and gaming logistics.

Gemini: Employed with prompt engineering, narrative strategy development, and structuring dialogue interactive framework.

Adobe Illustrator: Design and vectorize all custom graphics, character portraits and UI assets.

HTML5: Provided structure for screens, cinematic dialogues, and minigame containers.

CSS3: Visual styling, retro Codec aesthetic, CRT screen effects, and layout for minigames.

JavaScript (Vanilla): Control logic, state machine for missions, typewriter effect, and interactive event management without heavy frameworks.

Web Audio API: Used to generate retro sound effects and audio feedback for dialogues and minigames.

This project is creative as it has taken a series of scientific documents released by NASA and transformed them into an experience where children are able to learn that same information in a fun and interactive manner. Our team considered the lack of reading in young children, and is aiming to improve reading statistics and comprehension.
